title: Authorities disrupt nearly 11,000 cybercrime networks in Africa
description: Operation Serengeti III was a coordinated law enforcement effort across 21 African countries that disrupted nearly 11,000 cybercriminal networks and arrested over 1,400 suspects involved in business email compromise, ransomware, online scams, and other cybercrimes. The operation recovered more than $105 million in illegal funds and identified over 65,000 victims with estimated losses exceeding $385 million. Notable actions included dismantling fraud rings in Uganda, seizing illegal cryptocurrency mining equipment in Angola, and arresting a suspect in Nigeria linked to a large-scale phishing and business email compromise campaign. Private cybersecurity firms provided critical intelligence to support the operation. This large-scale crackdown highlights ongoing efforts to combat cybercrime in Africa but does not describe a specific vulnerability or exploit.
aiSummary: Operation Serengeti III was a multinational law enforcement initiative coordinated by Interpol involving 21 countries and private cybersecurity partners. The operation targeted cybercriminal networks engaged in business email compromise, ransomware, online scams, fraudulent mobile lending apps, vehicle import fraud, and cryptocurrency scams. It resulted in the arrest of 1,462 suspects, dismantling of 10,909 malicious networks, and recovery of over $105 million in illicit funds. Intelligence from private firms helped identify attacker infrastructure such as suspicious domains, IP addresses, and command-and-control servers. The operation also uncovered illegal cryptocurrency mining centers and large-scale phishing campaigns. While impactful, this event is a law enforcement action against cybercrime rather than a technical vulnerability or exploit.
aiImpact: The operation disrupted a significant number of cybercriminal networks and arrested many suspects, reducing the operational capacity of these groups in Africa. It helped recover substantial illicit funds and exposed widespread victimization affecting tens of thousands of individuals and organizations. The takedown of infrastructure and arrests likely degraded ongoing cybercrime activities such as business email compromise, ransomware deployment, phishing, and cryptocurrency fraud in the region. However, no specific technical vulnerability or exploit was disclosed or mitigated as part of this operation.
